definition: Procedures whose rules produce the same result when started with the same inputs and conditions.
example: A simulation test uses a fixed initial state to reproduce the same predicted trajectory.

definition: A lawn maintenance machine that loosens and removes accumulated dead stems and roots above the soil.
example: A groundskeeper removes a thick layer of thatch before overseeding.

definition: An approach to education that adapts teaching to learners' developmental stage, individual needs, and cultural context.
example: An early childhood teacher uses manipulatives and play to introduce counting.

definition: A family of software component libraries for building user interfaces, reports, and data visualizations.
example: A developer adds a DevExpress data grid with sorting to a business application.

definition: Determining the causes, impact, and context of a departure from an approved procedure or expected result.
example: A quality specialist reviews batch records and interviews operators after a process check fails.

definition: A formal process for recording, assessing, investigating, and resolving departures from established requirements.
example: A quality team logs a deviation, assesses affected products, and tracks corrective actions to closure.

definition: An approach that combines development and operations practices to deliver and operate software collaboratively and reliably.
example: A team shares deployment ownership and uses automation to release and monitor new versions.

definition: An approach that integrates security practices and responsibilities throughout collaborative software delivery and operation.
example: A team includes dependency review and security checks alongside its normal release checks.

definition: Interpreting evidence to identify factors that explain an observed condition or performance problem.
example: An analyst compares system measurements before and after an incident to identify its likely cause.

definition: Google's platform for building conversational interfaces that interpret user requests and manage responses.
example: A support team configures a chatbot to distinguish billing questions from service outages.

definition: A device used to record spoken material, especially for transcription.
example: A reporter records spoken notes and transcribes them later.
sense_note: The name originated as a brand and is also used generically.

definition: Speaking material aloud clearly and in a structured sequence for recording or transcription.
example: A clinician dictates encounter notes for authorized transcription.

definition: Designing or assessing digital content and interfaces so people with disabilities can use them.
example: A designer verifies that a registration form can be completed with a keyboard and a screen reader.

definition: Planning, placing, and evaluating paid promotional messages across digital channels.
example: A campaign manager compares the cost per registration from search and display ads.

definition: A software platform and product family for managing aspects of enterprise application development and delivery.
example: A release manager uses the platform to coordinate approvals across several application teams.

definition: Creating and managing messages and interactions distributed through digital channels.
example: A school coordinates an announcement across its website, email, and text alerts.

definition: Defining how an organization will attract, serve, and retain customers through digital channels.
example: A retailer maps where customers abandon online orders and prioritizes checkout improvements.

definition: Using digital tools and information adaptively and confidently to accomplish tasks and solve unfamiliar problems.
example: An employee chooses a suitable online collaboration tool and teaches coworkers how to use it.

definition: Reporting, verifying, producing, and publishing journalism in digital formats and channels.
example: A reporter publishes a verified local election story with interactive precinct results.

definition: Presenting and organizing products in digital storefronts to help shoppers discover and evaluate them.
example: A retailer adjusts product categories and featured items on an online storefront.

definition: A signaling standard that supports interoperable call-control features between private telephone exchanges.
example: A company links participating office exchanges so employees can use internal calling features.

definition: The ability to use digital devices, software, and online services to complete practical tasks safely and effectively.
example: A worker organizes shared documents and adjusts their permissions for collaborators.

definition: Redesigning organizational processes, services, or business models around digital technologies and data.
example: A hospital replaces a paper referral workflow with a system shared by participating clinics.

definition: An algorithm for finding shortest paths from a source in a graph whose edge weights are nonnegative.
example: A routing system computes the least-cost paths from a depot using nonnegative road distances.

definition: A software configuration management tool for controlling source versions, baselines, and changes.
example: A release engineer records which component versions belong to an approved baseline.

definition: Microsoft interfaces that allow compatible hardware to accelerate video decoding and other video processing on Windows.
example: A media player delegates supported decoding work to the graphics hardware.
sense_note: An API technology, not a standalone video player library.

definition: Guiding others as they learn and practice the teachings of a religious tradition, commonly Christianity.
example: A mentor leads regular discussions about applying shared beliefs in everyday situations.
sense_note: The scope depends on the community and tradition.

definition: Handling disagreements by documenting issues, managing communications, and pursuing an appropriate resolution.
example: A contract manager coordinates records and discussions for a disputed invoice before mediation.

definition: Delivering instruction and supporting learning when participants and instructors are not in the same physical location.
example: A teacher combines streamed lessons and asynchronous assignments for remote students.

definition: Solving a problem by splitting it into smaller instances, solving those instances, and combining their results.
example: Merge sort divides a list, sorts each part, and merges the sorted lists.

definition: An aviation software assurance standard that defines objectives for developing and verifying airborne software.
example: An avionics supplier traces safety-related requirements to their software verification evidence.

definition: A platform and toolset for building, distributing, and running applications in containers.
example: A team packages a service and its dependencies in a container image for deployment.

definition: A family of standards governing data communications over cable television networks.
example: A cable modem exchanges broadband data with the operator's network using a supported DOCSIS version.

definition: Examining collected documents to extract, organize, and assess information relevant to an authorized investigation or analysis.
example: An analyst records dates and identifies corroborating records from an authorized document collection.

definition: An electronic signature and digital agreement platform used to route documents for approval, signing, and tracking.
example: A contracting team sends an approved agreement for electronic signatures and records its completion.

definition: A family of United States Department of Defense directives and instructions concerning information assurance and cybersecurity.
sense_note: Confirm the particular documents and historical version because the series has evolved.

definition: A former Department of Defense process for evaluating information system security controls and authorizing systems to operate.
sense_note: Historical process often abbreviated DIACAP; do not present as the current authorization workflow.

definition: A Department of Defense instruction establishing how the Risk Management Framework is applied to covered information systems.
sense_note: Check the applicable edition when a precise requirement is relevant.

definition: A Department of Defense architecture framework for describing organizational capabilities, operations, systems, and their relationships through structured views.
example: An architect shows which systems support a military organization's information exchanges.

definition: A JavaScript templating library that generates text or markup by applying templates to data.
example: A developer renders a list of records into HTML using a compiled template.
